name: Speedy Go
author: Code and core

sections.description:
SpeedyGo is an all-in-one performance plugin for WordPress, designed to optimize every aspect of your site’s speed and efficiency. It features full-page caching, HTML/CSS/JS minification and combination, browser and object caching, Gzip & Brotli compression, lazy loading, mobile-specific caching, built-in CDN support, cache preloading, scheduled expiration, and advanced cache rules.

Free Features

Caching & Performance

  • Full-Page Caching: Cache entire pages for instant delivery, with options for cache expiry, exclusions, and auto-purge.
  • Cache Expiry & Auto Purge: Set cache expiration rules and automatically purge outdated cache files.
  • Exclude URLs: Define URLs to be excluded from caching.
  • Browser Caching: Leverage browser cache to reduce load times.
  • Global CDN: Free built-in CDN support for lightning-fast asset delivery.

Asset Optimization

  • HTML Minification: Reduce HTML file size for faster rendering.
  • CSS & JS Minification: Minify CSS and JavaScript files for optimal delivery.
  • Gzip & Brotli Compression: Compress files for improved speed.

User Experience & Admin Tools

  • Admin Dashboard Widget: Monitor cache status from the dashboard.
  • User-Friendly Admin Interface: Modern, easy-to-use settings and management screens.
  • Admin Bar Integration: Quick access to cache purging, optimization presets, and settings from the admin bar.
  • Settings API Integration: All options are managed via the WordPress Settings API for reliability and security.
  • AJAX Bulk Actions: All bulk actions and progress checks are handled via secure AJAX endpoints.
  • System Info Tab: View server and plugin environment details.
  • Uninstall Cleanup: On uninstall, all plugin-created cache and database tables are removed.

Pro Features

🌟 Upgrade to SpeedyGo Pro

Advanced Caching

  • Object Caching: Speed up dynamic content using object cache and transients.
  • Database Query Caching: Optimize repeated database queries.
  • Mobile Caching: Serve optimized cache for mobile users, with advanced rules.
  • Cache Preloading & Warm-Up: Automatically preload and warm up cache for improved response times.
  • Scheduled Expiration: Automate cache expiration to keep content fresh.
  • Advanced Cache Rules: Fine-tune caching with advanced rules and exclusions.

Advanced Asset Optimization

  • CSS & JS Combination: Combine multiple CSS/JS files to reduce HTTP requests.
  • Exclude CSS/JS Files: Exclude specific files from minification or combination.
  • Critical CSS Generation: Automated Critical CSS generation and async stylesheet loading.
  • Image Optimization (WebP): Advanced image optimization features.
  • Exclusive CDN Storage: Premium CDN storage with dedicated resources for your static assets.
  • Lazy Loading: Defer offscreen images for faster initial page loads.

User Experience & Developer Tools

  • Custom Cron Schedules: Register and use custom cron intervals for cache processing.
  • Debug Tools & Logging: Advanced debug logging and error tracking for troubleshooting.
  • Priority Support: Exclusive access to priority developer support.

Usage

  • Enable/disable features as needed from the settings page.
  • Monitor progress and logs from the dashboard widget and debug tools.
  • Use the admin bar for quick cache purging, applying an optimization preset, and access to settings.

Third Party / External Services

This plugin connects to external services. By installing and activating this plugin you agree to the terms and privacy policies listed below.

SpeedyGo (https://speedygo.io)

The plugin communicates with speedygo.io for the following purposes:

  1. License validation – Once per day via WordPress Cron the plugin sends your site URL, domain name, and license key to speedygo.io to confirm your subscription is active. No visitor personal data is included.
  2. Settings synchronisation – When you save settings in the SpeedyGo dashboard, configuration data is pushed from speedygo.io to your site via a cryptographically signed webhook. When you apply a preset from the plugin, your settings are likewise sent back to speedygo.io so the dashboard stays in sync.
  3. Account connection – When you click “Connect to SpeedyGo”, your browser opens a popup to speedygo.io to authenticate and select a plan. Your site URL and a one-time auth token are included in the URL.
  4. Usage telemetry (opt-in only) – If you choose to share anonymous usage data during connection, aggregate plugin-feature events are sent to speedygo.io. This is optional and can be declined or withdrawn at any time.

Data transmitted to speedygo.io: WordPress site URL, domain name, license key, plugin version. No visitor names, email addresses, or IP addresses are ever transmitted.

  • Privacy Policy: https://speedygo.io/privacy-policy/
  • Terms of Service: https://speedygo.io/terms-of-service/

Bunny.net CDN (only when CDN features are enabled)

When CDN delivery is active, static assets are served from Bunny.net pull zones managed by SpeedyGo. Bunny.net may log standard web-server data (IP address, user agent, requested URL) per its own privacy policy.

  • Privacy Policy: https://bunny.net/privacy/
  • Terms of Service: https://bunny.net/tos/

Privacy Policy

When the plugin is connected to a SpeedyGo account it transmits your WordPress site URL, domain name, and license key to speedygo.io for license validation and settings synchronisation. No visitor personal data (names, email addresses, IP addresses) is collected or transmitted by this plugin. Anonymous usage telemetry is strictly opt-in and can be declined or withdrawn at any time from the plugin settings.

Full privacy policy: https://speedygo.io/privacy-policy/

sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin files to /wp-content/plugins/speedy-go or install via the WordPress plugins screen.
  2. Activate the plugin through the ‘Plugins’ screen in WordPress.
  3. Go to Settings → SpeedyGo to configure caching and optimization settings.
sections.faq:
Does this plugin require special server configuration?

No, SpeedyGo works with standard WordPress installations. For best results, use PHP 7.2+.

Can I exclude specific files or URLs from caching or minification?

Yes, you can define exclusions for caching, minification, and combination in the settings.

Is SpeedyGo compatible with WooCommerce?

Yes, it automatically bypasses caching for WooCommerce dynamic pages like Cart, Checkout, and My Account.

Will this plugin break my site’s design?

It shouldn’t! However, if you notice any visual issues after enabling CSS/JS minification or combination, you can easily exclude specific files or disable those specific features in the settings while keeping caching active.

How do I clear the cache?

You can quickly purge the entire cache from the SpeedyGo item in the WordPress admin bar, or from the plugin’s settings page.

Will I get free CDN in this plugin?

Yes you get the CDN support with free version and with paid version you will get exclusive CDN storage.

Will this plugin improve my Google Core Web Vitals?

Yes, by optimizing LCP (Largest Contentful Paint) and other key metrics through caching, minification, and deferred asset loading, SpeedyGo is designed to directly improve your Core Web Vitals score.

Is SpeedyGo suitable for high-traffic websites?

Absolutely. Its advanced full-page caching and query optimization are built to scale, ensuring your server remains stable even during massive traffic spikes.

What is the difference between SpeedyGo Free and Pro?

The free version offers essential full-page caching and minification. The Pro version unlocks advanced features like automated Critical CSS generation, image optimization (WebP), advanced mobile caching rules, and priority support.

Why aren’t my changes showing up after editing a page?

SpeedyGo automatically purges the cache when you update a post or page. If your changes don’t appear, try manually clearing the cache via the admin bar. Also, ensure you don’t have a separate server-level cache or CDN cache that needs to be cleared.

Is SpeedyGo compatible with page builders like Elementor or Divi?

Yes, it works seamlessly with popular page builders. If you experience visual anomalies after an update, you may need to clear the builder’s internal cache alongside SpeedyGo’s cache.

How does the ‘Preload Cache’ feature work?

It automatically visits your pages in the background so that the cache is already generated before a real visitor arrives, ensuring the fastest possible load times.

Does this plugin support WordPress Multisite?

Yes, SpeedyGo is fully compatible with WordPress Multisite networks. You can network-activate it or activate it on individual sub-sites.
sections.changelog:
2.1.13

  • New: Analytics and marketing tags installed as inline snippets (Google Tag Manager, GA4, Facebook Pixel, Microsoft Clarity, Snapchat, Hotjar) are now delayed until the visitor interacts – previously only externally loaded tags were. Their events queue and send when the tag loads, so nothing is lost.
  • New: Google reCAPTCHA loads only when the visitor first interacts instead of on every page view, saving around 500 KB of JavaScript on pages with a form. Forms always work – any interaction (or the delay timeout) loads it long before a visitor can reach the Submit button.
  • Fix: The “site design looks different on the first visit, fixes itself after a refresh” issue. Critical CSS now remembers which stylesheets it was learned from and relearns automatically when the site’s CSS changes, instead of serving a stale design.
  • Improved: Critical CSS is captured only after the page has fully settled (fonts loaded, browser idle), producing more accurate above-the-fold styling.
  • New: Google Fonts and Bunny Fonts stylesheets no longer block the first paint – text shows immediately in a fallback font and swaps in when the webfont arrives.
  • New: Lazy-loaded images now tell the browser to download the image size that matches their real layout box, so phones stop downloading desktop-sized files.
  • New: Option to remove the legacy jQuery Migrate script from the front end (off by default – enable it from the dashboard).
  • Fix: Empty stylesheets and scripts are no longer served as real requests – each one was a wasted render-blocking download on some sites.

2.1.12

  • Fix: Connecting on sites behind a firewall or security plugin could get stuck in a loop. The connection now completes reliably by fetching the key outbound, and if it still cannot, clear manual steps are shown instead of looping.
  • Fix: Critical CSS could fail to switch on, leaving stylesheets blocking the page. It now activates reliably and moves your full stylesheets off the render-blocking path.
  • Fix: Page-builder scripts (Elementor, Divi and similar) are now deferred where it is safe to, instead of being left to block the page. They are still never minified or combined.
  • Fix: Videos and Google Maps built with Elementor – and maps in the common “output=embed” form – now load only when clicked, instead of loading their full player on every visit.
  • Fix: Lazy load no longer changes markup that lives inside inline scripts, so sliders and galleries that build their own image tags keep working.
  • Fix: The WebP “images converted” count and savings now reflect what a visitor actually downloads, and the conversion limit is applied exactly.
  • New: “Go to Dashboard” now signs you straight into your SpeedyGo dashboard, with this site already selected – no separate login.
  • Improvement: Notices read like plain English, plus a range of stability and safety improvements throughout.

2.1.11

  • Fix: Sites using a custom PHP-session login were logged straight back out after signing in. Pages that rely on a PHP session are now never served from, or written to, the shared cache.
  • Fix: AJAX forms (login, add to cart, comments) could stop working on pages that had been cached for a long time. Pages that contain a security token are now refreshed before that token expires.
  • Fix: A broken logo or image when a cached .webp file was not a valid image. The original image is served instead and the bad file is removed automatically.
  • Fix: Layout shifting and slow loading when Critical CSS captured an incomplete stylesheet. An incomplete capture is now ignored, so stylesheets stay blocking (safe) instead of causing a flash of unstyled content.
  • Fix: A leftover file from a deleted caching plugin kept showing a false “other cache plugin” warning and blocked SpeedyGo’s own cache. It is now cleaned up automatically.
  • Fix: Self-heal error reports were being rejected, so a broken optimization was never switched off automatically. Reports now work on CDN-hosted sites and on long-lived cached pages.
  • New: Pages are rebuilt in the background right after a cache purge, so the first visitor after a purge is never slow.
  • New: Automatic compatibility with Elementor, Divi, WPBakery and Beaver Builder – their scripts are never minified, combined, deferred or delayed.
  • New: If an optimization causes a JavaScript error, it is switched off automatically and explained in an admin notice, with a one-click “Re-enable anyway”.
  • New: “Go to Dashboard” now opens the SpeedyGo dashboard with your site already selected.
  • New: Every cached page ends with a comment showing the plugin version and when the page was cached, which makes support much faster.
  • Improvement: JavaScript Minification is no longer enabled by the optimization presets. It remains available as an optional setting.

2.1.10

  • New: Critical CSS + async stylesheet loading (fixes render-blocking).
  • Fix: Defer being silently disabled on all minified scripts.
  • Enhancement: Added ‘Unlock Pro Version’ and ‘Need Developer Help?’ banners on the connection success page.
  • New: Self-heal safety net – If an optimized file throws a JS error, the plugin detects it and automatically switches that feature off on that site.
  • New: Kill switch / safe mode – Any feature can be disabled remotely per site end-to-end.
  • New: Stale-while-revalidate serving – Visitors always receive a cached page instantly while cache refreshes in the background.
  • New: Smart cache purges – Targeted, de-duplicated purges with a tag index replace blanket cache wipes.

2.1.9

  • New: Apply optimization presets (Starter, Moderate, Extensive) directly from the WordPress admin bar. Hover the SpeedyGo item, choose a preset, and it configures all your settings, purges the cache, and shows a live progress timeline – your choice also syncs to the SpeedyGo dashboard, so there is no need to open the dashboard.
  • Fix: Some connected sites were being automatically disconnected roughly a day after activation. License verification now disconnects a site only when its subscription is genuinely cancelled or expired (confirmed over several days). A signature or key mismatch, a host without the PHP sodium extension, a timeout, or any other temporary/technical error can no longer disconnect a working site – the plugin stays connected and simply retries.
  • Fix: Scheduled cache tasks that appeared as “Unknown schedule” with no action in cron tools (e.g. WP Crontrol) are now always registered correctly and clean themselves up when their feature is turned off, so no orphaned events remain.
  • Fix: Editing or updating a post now reliably clears that page’s cached copy.
  • New: Home-page image-optimization (WebP) savings are measured and reported to your SpeedyGo dashboard.
  • Improvement: Faster cache delivery – cached pages are stored pre-compressed (no per-request gzip), and the main above-the-fold image is prioritized (fetchpriority) for a quicker Largest Contentful Paint. After a purge or edit, visitors are served the previous cached page while the new one rebuilds in the background.
  • Improvement: Add ?nospeedygo to any URL to view the page with all SpeedyGo optimizations bypassed for that request (handy for support and debugging).
  • Compatibility: Tested with WordPress 7.0 and PHP 8.x.

2.1.8

  • New: Serves cache before WordPress fully loads (big TTFB win), with auto-rollback safety.

2.1.7

  • Fix: Button linking and some design fixes.

2.1.6

  • New: Added API detection to automatically notify users if another caching plugin is active, preventing conflicts.
  • Enhancement: Redesigned the admin connection page with a modern UI and manual connection fallback form.
  • Enhancement: Added active and hover state styling for the SpeedyGo admin menu.
  • Enhancement: Made the admin connection page WPML translation ready.
  • Cleanup: Removed unused promo banners and background images to reduce plugin footprint.

2.1.5

  • Fix: Removed a temporary debug block from the license validation flow that could leak raw database details (table name, query counts) inside the “Invalid license key” error shown on the Connect page. Added a safety net so debug output can never reach a customer’s screen again, even from a future server-side regression.
  • Fix: font-display: swap now correctly overrides an existing bad value (e.g. font-display: block or auto) shipped in a theme or third-party plugin’s own font CSS, instead of only applying when the property was missing entirely. Previously, a theme icon font or a service like Font Awesome that already set font-display: block would keep that value untouched, leaving the PageSpeed “Font display” warning in place even with this setting enabled.
  • Fix: Resolved “Mixed Content” errors that could block the plugin’s own generated CSS, JS, and WebP images on sites running behind a reverse proxy or CDN that terminates SSL upstream of the server (e.g. Cloudflare, a load balancer). Cache URLs are now correctly generated as https when the site is actually served over https, even when WordPress’s own SSL detection is inconclusive.

2.1.4

  • Fix: When both Gzip/Brotli compression and “Defer JS” were enabled at the same time, the defer attribute was silently never added to any script tag. Root cause: compression ran first, converting the HTML to binary bytes, then the defer pass couldn’t find any <script tags in the compressed data. Fixed by running defer (and all other HTML transformations) before compression. Cache files are now always written uncompressed; only the live HTTP response is compressed.

2.1.3

  • Fix: License activation now works correctly on hosts where the PHP sodium extension is not installed (e.g. shared hosting without libsodium). The plugin now requests an HMAC fallback from the server when sodium is unavailable, so verification succeeds without requiring a server-side extension change.
  • Fix: Resolved a false “Cryptographic signature verification failed / forge/tampering detected” error caused by a JSON encoding difference between the server (Node.js outputs raw Unicode) and PHP (escapes Unicode as \uXXXX). Verification now compares decoded data structures rather than raw byte strings, eliminating the mismatch.
  • Fix: Added dual-canonical HMAC verification – the plugin now tries both PHP-style and JS-style JSON encoding when verifying HMAC responses, preventing fallback failures on Unicode content.
  • Improvement: Verification error messages are now specific (key_mismatch, content_mismatch, no_sodium_no_hmac, hmac_failed) making it easier to diagnose connection issues.
  • Improvement: Plugin now sends X-Speedygo-Accept-HMAC header on every request, enabling HMAC fallback automatically when the server detects sodium is unavailable or keys are mismatched.
  • Tested up to WordPress 6.7.

2.1.2

  • Improvement: Free plugin detects and deactivates itself when the Pro version is active, preventing function conflicts.
  • Fix: Compatibility improvements for WAF-protected sites using outbound polling instead of inbound push for CDN sync.
  • Fix: CDN sync progress display for WAF sites.
  • Fix: Subscription domain check no longer incorrectly matches subdomains as the root domain.

2.1.1

  • Fix: Resolved all WordPress Plugin Check security, i18n, and coding standards issues.
  • Fix: Replaced parse_url() with wp_parse_url() across all files for consistent output.
  • Fix: Replaced fopen/fread/fclose with WP_Filesystem::get_contents() in cache serving.
  • Fix: Added missing translators comments and corrected mismatched text domains.
  • Fix: Prefixed global functions sg_* renamed to cnc_sg_* for WordPress namespace compliance.
  • Fix: Escaped all output in admin-connection.php (esc_url, esc_attr).
  • Fix: Replaced date() with gmdate() in settings export filename.
  • Fix: Replaced unlink() with wp_delete_file() in uninstall.php.
  • Fix: Gated all error_log() calls behind WP_DEBUG to remove debug code from production.
  • Tested up to WordPress 7.0.

2.0.3

  • New: Added “Exclude WooCommerce Default Pages” option to automatically bypass cache for Cart, Checkout, and My Account pages.
  • New: Implemented Import/Export settings tab for backup and migration support.
  • Enhancement: Refined settings UI with improved tab layout and background image support for WebP conversion.
  • Fix: Resolved “Bad Request” AJAX error in the API key manual connection form.
  • Fix: Resolved issue where settings failed to save due to nested HTML form elements.
  • Fix: Resolved Admin JS crash occurring on specific settings pages.
  • Fix: Resolved PHP errors/warnings related to deprecated functions.
  • Enhancement: Clarified “Exclude URLs” instructions to specify full URLs on new lines.

2.0.2

  • Minor UI refinements and styling adjustments.
  • Accessibility improvements for admin settings.
  • Updated compatibility for latest WordPress versions.

2.0.1

  • Tested up to: 6.9
  • Minor stability improvements.
  • Documentation updates.
  • Code cleanup and small performance refinements.

2.0.0

  • New: Added a comprehensive Telemetry tracking feature to monitor usage data, including an opt-in modal on activation and a dedicated tab in Settings.
  • New: Introduced a Deactivation Feedback modal to safely gather user insights when the plugin is deactivated.
  • Security: Resolved multiple WordPress Coding Standards (WPCS) security warnings, adding strict sanitization and nonce verification across admin functions.
  • Fix: Patched a bug in the deactivation flow where conflicting alerts overtook the custom feedback modal.
  • Enhancement: Refactored the plugin’s CSS and JS enqueuing logic to strictly load only on necessary admin pages, improving backward compatibility.
  • Cleanup: Removed outdated/redundant codebase files and cleaned up the overall plugin footprint.

1.0.0

  • Initial release
